source.title: Unifying Attention Heads and Task Vectors via Hidden State Geometry in In-Context Learning
source.authors: Hao-Lin Yang; Hakaze Cho; Yi-Qiao Zhong; Naoya Inoue

page_placements.theme: Label-copying heads in few-shot classification ICL, and the failure modes they cause

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some figures and equations are flattened, but the relevant reported results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests induction-head contributions to in-context classification with attention-pattern scoring and head ablations, and tests related setup conditions, rather than reproducing training-time formation measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper studies inference-time hidden-state geometry and head ablations, not induction-head formation during training. It does not measure training loss bumps or token-index loss changes. Layerwise geometry figures describe a two-stage inference process, not when heads form during training. Rows below cover the reported head-ablation accuracies, relevant control and label-presence settings, and directly relevant geometric effects; cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: In pretrained Llama2, Llama3 and Gemma models (2B–70B), the study ablates the top 10% of heads ranked by an induction-style attention score (attention from the query ':' to earlier label tokens). It measures few-shot classification accuracy against PTH-ablation and random-head controls. That is a different method aimed at whether induction heads carry in-context learning in large models (V3), and whether few-shot learning runs mainly through other heads (V6). It has no training-time measurements, so V2, V5 and V7 are untested. V1 is untested because there are no small attention-only models and no test of PTH→IH composition.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that ICL improves classification mainly by improving alignment of query hidden states with label unembeddings, through a two-stage layer-wise process: early-layer PTHs drive separability and later-layer IHs drive alignment, which explains why IH outputs work as task vectors. They also say IH effectiveness depends on the query label being present in context; in that setting they report PTH ablation hurting more, though this holds clearly only for Llama2-70B and Llama3-70B. Training-time emergence is left to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretrained Llama and Gemma models, identifies heads by attention patterns, and ablates or injects head outputs while measuring classification accuracy and hidden-state geometry. It does not reproduce the original training-time induction-head emergence and loss measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Head-ablation effects vary with model and demonstration-label availability. In the no-matching-label Famous People setting, PTH ablation has a larger accuracy effect than IH ablation; in standard ICL, IH ablation has the larger effect. Random-head ablations also cause substantial accuracy changes in several reported model aggregates.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating PTHs mainly reduces hidden-state separability; ablating IHs leaves separability intact but disrupts alignment with label unembeddings (Llama2-70B, Figure 7; other models Figures 29–34).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In LLM classification ICL, previous-token heads build label separability in early layers and induction heads align hidden states with label unembeddings in later layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Summed IH outputs injected as task vectors at layer 30 raise Llama2-70B zero-shot accuracy from 0.24% to 65.11%; this works across models except Gemma-2B (Figures 9, 65–70).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-head outputs act as task vectors that steer zero-shot hidden states toward label directions.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to inference-time behavior in pretrained models and classification-focused tasks; the generation-task analysis is described as preliminary. Results are averaged across datasets for the main model comparisons, and numerical uncertainty estimates for the accuracy effects are not stated. Random-head ablation also has substantial reported effects in several models.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant quantitative results were omitted. Detailed layerwise geometry curves and many supplementary task-by-model plots are figure-only and do not measure training-time head formation, training loss bumps, or token-index loss; only the directly described Figure 7 geometric effects were retained.

untested.parts: All of it: no small attention-only models, no test that IHs compose with PTHs, no generic repeated-token [A][B]…[A]→[B] task.
All of it: no training-time measurements.
Loss falling with token index; the share of all ICL explained; non-classification tasks. Only few-shot classification accuracy is measured.
Other architectures and modalities; training-run variation; whether induction scores exceed a threshold. Heads are selected by top-10% ranking, which always returns heads.
All of it: only inference-time prompt manipulations, no training-data properties.
Few-shot tasks beyond classification and Famous People; mean or resample ablation instead of zeroing.
All of it: the 'phase transition' is across layers at inference, not across training.

missing.what: Zero-shot ablation control: IH ablation has practically no effect without demonstrations (0.24%→0.05%, random 0.08%, PTH 0.00%), so the IH effect is specific to ICL.
Layer positions of top IHs vs PTHs: IHs sit significantly later in all models (e.g. Llama2-70B 41.5 vs 35.9 at 10%, p≈1e-28), but not at the 1–2% levels in Llama3-70B (p=0.56, 0.13).

record.verdict_notes: The 'IHs' here are top-10% heads by attention from the final ':' to earlier label tokens, a looser criterion than the original prefix-matching score; they may overlap with function-vector heads. Ablation zeros outputs of 10% of all heads, and random controls of equal size cut accuracy by about 30–40 points in four models. Post-ablation accuracies near 0% match zero-shot levels (the model stops emitting label tokens), not chance. All V1 and V5 links in the record were removed: the models are large pretrained ones, and the manipulations are inference-time prompts, not training data.

versions.untested_parts: Tests induction-head behavior and contribution in pretrained Llama and Gemma classification models; does not test small attention-only transformers, formation through a specific previous-token-head composition, or the generic repeated-token [A][B] … [A] → [B] task.
No training-time head-formation measurements, training loss curve, or token-index in-context-learning loss measurement.
Does not measure loss falling with token index or estimate what proportion of large-transformer ICL that induction heads explain.
Tests Llama and Gemma model families at several sizes; does not test other architectures, modalities, or variation across training runs.
Tests inference-time demonstration configurations and label availability, not training-data properties or how training determines the time of head formation.

Compares PTH and IH ablations in classification settings, including a setting where the query label is absent from demonstrations; does not comprehensively test few-shot task learning across tasks or mechanisms.
The reported two-stage changes concern hidden-state geometry across inference layers, not a sequence of induction-head formation steps during training.

relationships.condition: Standard 8-shot classification ICL, all seven Llama2/Llama3/Gemma models (2B–70B)
relationships.reason: Zeroing top-10% IH outputs cuts accuracy to 0–5.7% from 66–81% (r01,r04,r07,r10,r13,r16,r19); random-head controls barely move in Llama2-70B, Llama2-13B and Llama3-70B (r03,r15,r09).
relationships.display_finding: Zeroing the top 10% of induction-head outputs reduced accuracy from 66–81% to 0–5.7%; random-head controls barely changed accuracy in Llama2-70B, Llama2-13B and Llama3-70B.

relationships.condition: Llama3-8B, Llama2-7B, Gemma-2B, Gemma-7B standard setting
relationships.reason: Random-head ablation of equal size also drops accuracy by 28–39 points (r06,r12,r18,r21), so part of the IH effect may be generic zero-ablation damage.
